I1.strategy: Reuse existing assets.frontend_closure_manifest (native schema unchanged) for a strictly typed binding-provenance manifest. write_extension_binding writes exact runtime binding then O_EXCL sibling controller-extension.closure.json with schema/extension FileSeal/binding FileSeal/bridge_bootstrap PathIdentity. No lifecycle registry. Caller supplies this exact sibling as frontend_closure_manifest.
I1.bootstrap_checks: Held bounded capture compares path/hash/bytes/mtime to supplied original FileBinding; uid=current, mode0700, regular singlelink. Manifest binds device/inode/mode/uid/size/hash/mtime. Frontend and process producers reopen and compare identity and runtime binding.command exactly. Native frontend validates manifest bytes; root process producer and full frontend SourceTree verify declared contents before execution.
I1.nonclaim: Manifest is binding provenance, not a substitute for the separately root-bound full frontend SourceTree. No new native keys/tool/provider/interface.

I2: Capture process exec/node/frontend/deployment under existing FileBinding authorities: equality of path/hash/size and mtime<=original, plus held capture checks. Serialize original mtime ceiling, not refreshed entitlement. Compare kernel/pyvenv captures to original frontend seals. Revalidate frontend/process config immediately before and after publication; any mutation denies, no re-seal.
I3: Frontend deployment direct child of artifact_root, never below session/tmp/profile/cwd. Process config outside all five sealed directory roots and asset directories whose closure it would change. Reject before publication; successful publication revalidates original frontend/process state. Preserve denied/partial files if publication later fails, no rollback/retry.
